results.name: Dumbbell Reverse Spider Curl
instructions: Begin by lying face down on an incline bench set at a 45-degree angle, with your chest supported on the bench and your forefeet planted firmly on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip (palms facing down), arms fully extended toward the floor.
Keep your upper arms stationary as you curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders, focusing on contracting your biceps.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, ensuring your elbows remain steady.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you curl the weights up and inhale as you lower them back down.
Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms throughout the exercise.
Keep your chest pressed against the bench to prevent any unnecessary movement.
results.description: Dumbbell Reverse Spider Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Brachialis, Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Seated Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, letting your arms hang down by your sides with your palms facing your body (neutral grip).
Keep your upper arms stationary and curl the dumbbells towards your shoulders by bending your elbows while rotating both wrists until your palms face the shoulders.
Squeeze your biceps at the peak of the movement and hold for a second.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Avoid swinging your arms or using momentum; focus on controlled, slow movements.
Exhale as you curl the dumbbells up and inhale as you lower them.
Concentrate on using your biceps to lift the weights, minimizing shoulder involvement.
results.description: Dumbbell Seated Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Seated Hammer Curl
instructions: Sit upright on a bench with your back on the backrest and feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, letting your arms hang down by your sides with your palms facing your body (neutral grip).
Begin the movement by bending your elbows, curling the dumbbells up towards your shoulders. Your palms should continue to face each other throughout the movement.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, ensuring the dumbbells reach shoulder height while keeping your elbows close to your body.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and pressed against the bench for stability.
Avoid swinging the weights or using momentum; focus on a controlled motion.
Exhale as you lift the dumbbells and inhale as you lower them.
results.description: Dumbbell Seated Hammer Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Seated Preacher Curl
instructions: Sit on a preacher bench with your chest against the support pad and your feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip (palms facing up).
Extend your arms fully over the preacher bench pad, allowing the dumbbells to hang down in front of you.
Curl the dumbbells upward towards your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary against the pad.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your upper arms pressed against the pad to isolate the biceps.
Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms.
Avoid locking your elbows at the bottom of the movement.
results.description: Dumbbell Seated Preacher Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Seated Reverse Grip Concentration Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your legs spread and your feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand with an overhand grip (palm facing down), lean forward and place your right elbow against the inside of your right thigh.
Allow the dumbbell to hang straight down towards the floor while keeping your arm fully extended.
Curl the dumbbell upward towards your shoulder by bending your elbow, focusing on engaging your biceps and forearms.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on squeezing your biceps and forearms at the top of the curl.
Ensure your wrist remains straight and aligned with your forearm.
Start with a lighter weight to ensure proper form.
results.description: Dumbbell Seated Reverse Grip Concentration Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Seated Zottman Curl
instructions: Sit upright on a bench with your feet firmly planted on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand by your sides using an underhand grip.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and curl both dumbbells toward your shoulders without moving your upper arms.
At the top, rotate both hands into an overhand grip, then slowly lower the dumbbells until your arms are fully extended.
Rotate your hands back into an underhand grip at the bottom, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms still.
Curl the dumbbells without swinging your shoulders or leaning forward.
Keep your wrists straight and rotate back to an underhand grip only after fully extending your arms.
Exhale as you curl the dumbbells and inhale as you lower them.
results.description: Dumbbell Seated Zottman Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Dumbbell Simultaneous Biceps Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms fully extended and palms facing forward.
Simultaneously curl both dumbbells upward towards your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, ensuring the dumbbells reach shoulder height.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your upper arms stationary and avoid swinging the weights.
Avoid using momentum; focus on using your biceps to lift the weights.
Exhale as you curl the weights up and inhale as you lower them.
results.description: Dumbbell Simultaneous Biceps Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Standing Concentration Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand. Slightly bend your knees and lean your torso forward, placing your left hand on your left knee for support. Allow your right arm to hang straight down towards the floor.
Curl the dumbbell towards your opposite shoulder by bending your elbow, keeping your upper arm stationary.
Squeeze your biceps at the peak of the movement, ensuring the dumbbell reaches close to your shoulder.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
tips: Keep your upper arm stationary throughout the exercise to isolate the biceps.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement.
Avoid using momentum to lift the dumbbell.
results.description: Dumbbell Standing Concentration Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Standing Hammer Drag Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other). Let the dumbbells hang by your sides.
Drag the dumbbells upward keeping the dumbbells close to your torso by pulling your elbows backward while lifting.
Continue dragging the dumbbells until they reach the level of your lower chest, squeezing your biceps at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on dragging the dumbbells upward, not curling them in a traditional manner.
Maintain a neutral grip and keep the dumbbells close to your body.
Breathe out as you lift the dumbbells and inhale as you lower them.
results.description: Dumbbell Standing Hammer Drag Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Standing One Arm Concentration Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand. Bend your knees and hinge to your hips to lean forward and place your right elbow on the inside of your right thigh and your left hand on your left knee for support.
Curl the dumbbell upward towards your shoulder by bending your elbow, focusing on engaging your biceps.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, ensuring the dumbbell reaches shoulder height.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position, fully extending your arm. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left arm.
tips: Focus on isolating the biceps and minimizing movement in your shoulder.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbow to avoid locking out the joint.
Breathe out as you curl the dumbbell and inhale as you lower it.
results.description: Dumbbell Standing One Arm Concentration Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.
